scenario: AITA for 'stealing' my Dad's business idea and making a success of it? | Title says it all really. I (26M) technically ''stole'' my dad's business idea. When I first heard it from him, it was so simple yet so...genius. I can't say exactly what it is here, but it was genius. The thing is, me and my dad (55M) are complete opposites. He's the more introverted and quiet type. He's always been *very* intelligent, but he's lacked the ability to *get things done.* I've been told I'm more like my grandad (75M, my dad's dad). Physically, I look more like my grandad, but personality wise, I guess I'm a bit more impulsive and hot headed and not as intelligent as my dad, but I get things done. Perhaps I'm more ''traditional masculine'' than my dad. Its like I should be in the older generation, and he should be from the newer one. When I heard my Dad's business idea, I was amazed, but I didn't truly believe my Dad could pull it off. He doesn't get things done. He's always been full of great ideas, but ideas not put to use are useless. So I took the idea and ran with it. I got IP rights and started the business with it 2 years ago. Since then, its been a massive success. Not millions or anything, but into the six figures and the potential to make millions is there perhaps in the next half decade if things keep going well. My dad was very upset when I did this, but didn't say much. I could tell by his facial expressions. My mom (55F) said I've done her proud and done the right thing. Well I confronted my dad yesterday to ask him how he feels and he said I'm a ''fucking asshole''. He said he felt betrayed by me and nearly started crying. I told him straight, ''You've always been a man of ideas, but I'm a man of action''. Then my sister (28F) walks in and starts saying shit to me, defending my dad. Both my mom and granddad have taken my side. I even offered my dad 20% of all profits, but he rejected and told me to get out. I understand why he's upset, but I think he's being unreasonable here. AITA?

message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether it's right or wrong for this person to take their dad's business idea and run with it, making a success out of it. The person is 26 years old, and their dad is 55. They describe their dad as introverted and intelligent but not someone who gets things done. On the other hand, they see themselves as more impulsive and hot-headed but capable of taking action. They took the idea, got IP rights, and started a business that's been successful, making six figures and with potential to make millions in the next few years. The dad was upset when he found out, and the person confronted him, telling him that he's a man of ideas while they're a man of action. The dad called them a "fucking asshole" and felt betrayed. The sister also defended the dad, while the mom and granddad supported the person. The person offered the dad 20% of the profits, but the dad refused and told them to get out. So, is this person AITA (Acting In Their Own Favour, but maybe not in a morally right way)? Or is it justified because they took action where their dad couldn't? First, I need to understand the dynamics between the person and their dad. The dad has great ideas but doesn't execute them, while the person is more action-oriented. The person saw the potential in the idea and decided to take it upon themselves to make it a reality. They secured IP rights, which shows they were serious about protecting the idea and their work. However, the dad felt betrayed because the person took his idea without his consent. The person didn't discuss the idea with the dad or seek his permission before moving forward. This lack of communication likely contributed to the dad's feelings of betrayal and hurt. On the other hand, the person's actions led to a successful business, which benefits not just themselves but potentially the family as well. They offered to share the profits, which shows willingness to compensate the dad for the idea. But the dad's refusal and emotional reaction suggest that it's not just about the money; it's about the principle of the idea being taken without his involvement. I also need to consider cultural and familial expectations. In some cultures, respecting elders and their ideas is paramount, and taking an idea without permission could be seen as disrespectful. In others, entrepreneurship and initiative are highly valued, and the person's actions might be seen as commendable. Another angle is the concept of intellectual property. If the dad shared the idea with the person, does the person have the right to use it? Or should they have sought permission or partnership before proceeding? Legally, if the dad didn't protect the idea with IP rights, the person might have been within their rights to use it. But morally, the lack of communication could be seen as wrong. Additionally, the person's offer to share profits shows a willingness to acknowledge the dad's contribution, but the dad's refusal indicates that financial compensation isn't enough to heal the relationship. The emotional and relational impact might be more significant than the financial success. In summary, while the person's actions led to a successful business, the lack of communication and the emotional impact on the dad make the situation more complex. It's not purely right or wrong; it depends on the values and expectations within their family and culture, as well as the importance of communication and respect for others' ideas.
